claim: Row (a) of the way-and-channel table (base l. 2582) rules 'S7's quay, intervallum or castle path': each crosses the under-deck strip only by the crossing rule, and on failure ends 'at the strip as at a reservation'. §4.8's lead (l. 7692) restates this for 'a quay, the intervallum or a castle path', §4.3 (l. 5749) for 'S7's quays, intervallum and castle paths', and V11 row 80 lists the castle paths among `clearWidthM`'s readers. The row's test cell is 'T110-2 (3), (5)'. T110-2 (3) (l. 18562–18563) runs the intervallum, and (5) (l. 18586–18587) runs a quay. No clause in the set runs a castle path, meaning §4.8's internal paths (keep ↔ gatehouse ↔ wall stairs, l. 7762), crossing or ending at an under-deck strip; a search of the base and the volumes for 'castle path' or 'internal path' finds only the rule sites. The case is reachable on a common path. An aqueduct crosses a castle's bailey *over the band*, and S7 lays the internal paths after it: at generation where the S6 aqueduct crosses the bailey, and at every Regenerate (keep) of a document with a declared aqueduct there. A build that lays a castle path along the strip, or through a support ring, passes every bar. Under principle (11) and R6-01's grading, a defined edge that no bar runs is MAJOR.
required_change: §13.2's T110-2 (3), after "… no ramp, stair or foot in the band or the channel, the stage's `N_k` gates on ground part 0;" (the clause's end, before "(4) *beneath* by hand"), add: "and a CITY fixture holding a declared masonry aqueduct across a corner of a castle's bailey (*over the band*), regenerated (keep), so that S7 lays the castle's internal paths (keep ↔ gatehouse ↔ wall stairs, §4.8) after it: each path crossing the under-deck strip under a span §4.3 admits or ending at the strip as at a reservation, 0 path corridors over a support ring, ramp, stair, foot or `vault` span's strip (§2.7's way-and-channel table, row a);".

claim:
§2.7's crossing table states the held raised way's meeting (column C8: "held (locked, pinned or declared) — as C2, a lock or pin never refusing work that passes beneath (§7.1's lock row)") for every wall event. Each cell names the test that runs it. In the hand and conversion rows, the named test never locks the raised way for that op:
| cell (base l.) | outcome | test named | what the test runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| W4·C8 (l. 2701) | *unchanged meeting* | T114-3 | the neglected ring's decay beneath a standing aqueduct (l. 18667–18669), unlocked |
| W7·C8 (l. 2704) | "as C2, no `refuse.locked`" | T110-2 (8) | `wallToWay` of (3)'s ring under an unlocked viaduct (l. 18615–18618); T-V6-47, which takes (8), unlocked too |
| W10·C8 (l. 2707) | as C2 | T114-3 | no `repairWall` beneath a locked raised way; its landfall clause repairs under an unlocked one |
| W11·C8 (l. 2708) | as C2 | T110-2 (4) | "a hand `delete` of a run beneath a standing viaduct" (l. 18574–18575), unlocked |
| W13·C8 (l. 2710) | "as C2, no `refuse.locked`" | T110-2 (4) | "a hand `placeGate` inside a viaduct's under-deck strip" (l. 18581–18582), unlocked |
T110-2 (4) runs its locked and pinned cases for the epoch circuits, the contraction and the two hand `drawWall`s only. It reads: "each run again with the raised way locked and with it pinned: no `refuse.locked`". T110-2 (5) does the same for hand roads and carves, and T-V9-52 for a wall drawn across a locked viaduct.
The lock check is a refusal path of its own: §7.1's lock row (l. 10631). That row refuses "a map event … crosses, targets or moves a locked or pinned entity". It exempts "a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck". §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10674) names "a `placeGate` inside its under-deck strip, locked, pinned or neither". A `convert`'s dry-run re-route (`wallToWay`), a `delete` and a `breach` or `dismantle` of the run beneath, a `repairWall` and a gate stub are each a different path into that check. A build that applies the exemption only to drawn ways and wall strokes refuses them under a locked raised way. That build passes every bar.
R6-01's grading: an edge the text defines but no bar runs, so that a wrong build passes every bar, is MAJOR. The cells also name a test that does not hold their case (round-6 note (6) (b) (i)).

claim:
In the crossing table's hand and conversion rows that this seat's tests hold, the other raised-way states name a clause that runs only C2 (the standing raised way):
- **W4** (`DeclineOp`'s `breach` or `dismantle`, l. 2701), C3–C6, C10, C12 and C13: "*unchanged meeting* · T114-3". T114-3 runs the epoch decay beneath a standing aqueduct (a `breach` by neglect) and its landfall clause. It runs no `breach` or `dismantle` beneath a raised way whose span has fallen, whose support is cleared, whose `vault` span is breached, which was repaired or extended, or whose spacing was edited. Even W4·C2's `dismantle` is held only by T-V6-11's `absorbWall`, which the cell does not name.
- **W7** (`wallToWay`, l. 2704), C3–C6, C10, C12 and C13: "as C2 · T110-2 (8)". (8) re-routes the ring road under a standing viaduct only. The row's outcome reads the crossing rule at that state, and V04 lays again "an arch vault the old wall stood over".
- **W10** (`repairWall`, l. 2707), C3–C6, C10, C12 and C13: "as C2 · T114-3". C2's own clause, "the bend's new stretch is a wall laid after: W2·C2 · T114-3, T-V6-11", is not held either. T-V6-11's repair on a dismantled stretch has no raised way over it. T114-3 repairs only a `breached` run under its landfall.
- **W11** (a hand `delete`, l. 2708) and **W13** (a hand `placeGate`, l. 2710), C3–C6, C10, C12 and C13: "as C2 · T110-2 (4)". (4)'s delete and gate cases have a standing viaduct only.
Each outcome is defined, and by construction it is C2's: the op writes its own records and the run's cap is read by *beneath*. So the class is the one VV56-r6-03 (rows W5, W6, W8) and VAL-R6-06 (row W9) raise, graded minor. V05 met the rule for row W12 with one T-V5-14 passage, run on each state in turn. These rows have none.

The crossing table's row W3, "a regeneration re-deriving a ring under a held raised way" (base l. 2700), names T110-2 (6) as the test of its cells C3 (one span fallen), C4 (all fallen), C5 (a support cleared or toppled), C6 (a `vault` span breached) and C10–C13. T110-2 (6) (l. 18598–18607) regenerates only standing held raised ways. At generation every raised way is new, so a regeneration is the only time S3's and S5a's pull, S4's crossing rule, S10's band and V04's T2 vaults step meet fallen parts and must read a `ruined` stump as impassable, a `cleared` ring as open ground, the clear width between standing rings only, the run at its own top beneath a fallen span and no chamber in a breached span. T110-2 (7) runs V06's epoch cost field, T110-2 (4) the hand operator's local bend and T-V6-47 the epoch re-solve, so a generation-path build that reads every recorded support as standing passes every bar, and at Regenerate (keep) or New random of a town whose held aqueduct has lapsed it routes the ring round a cleared support or caps a run at a fallen soffit.

claim: Cells of §2.7's crossing table name tests that never run their case. (1) W3·C3-C6 (l. 2700): a regeneration re-deriving a ring under a held raised way whose span fell, whose support was cleared or toppled, or whose `vault` span was breached. Each cell reads '*beneath* as read · T110-2 (6)', but T110-2 (6) (l. 18598-18607) regenerates only standing raised ways ((1)'s aqueduct and (3)'s viaduct, locked). The fallen-part readings run only on the epoch path (T110-2 (7), T-V6-47, through V06's cost field). So the generation path that reads `state` is never run: S5a's pull treating a `cleared` ring as open ground and a `ruined` aqueduct support as impassable (§4.4 S5a *Trace* (2)), and S10's band whole across a cleared footprint. A pull that ignores `state` passes every bar. (2) W7·C2 (l. 2704): its outcome includes 'V04 lays again an arch vault the old wall stood over · T110-2 (8), T-V6-47'. Neither T110-2 (8) (l. 18615-18618) nor T-V6-47's `wallToWay` clause has a `vault` span under the ring, and T-V4-63 runs the re-lay only for a hand delete. A `wallToWay` that leaves the chamber unlaid, or lays it under the ring road's corridor, passes every bar — exactly the case where the re-laid vault makes the strip impassable again and row (c)'s re-route must avoid it. Under R6-01's grading, a defined edge that no bar runs, so that a wrong build passes, is MAJOR.

claim: The crossing table's column C13 (base l. 2676–2681) gives the outcome of a raised way edited by its own op — 'a hand re-shape of its course, `spanSpacingCm` (V09's Arch spacing) or `clearanceCm` (Deck height)'. Its outcomes are: a station in a band laid after the deck slides off it; 'a re-shaped aqueduct stretch across a standing band *over the band*'; and 'a re-shaped road deck stretch across a standing trace bent down before it (`bend.raised.wall`)'. W1·C13 names T110-2 (4) as its test (l. 2698), and W2·C13 reads 'as W1·C13 · T110-2 (4)'. T110-2 (4) (l. 18582–18583) runs only the Arch-spacing case ('the viaduct's Arch spacing changed after the wall was drawn — its station in the band slid off it, the band whole there'). No bar in the set runs a re-shape (V04's `moveVertex`, V04 l. 372) across a standing wall: T-V9-52 runs a raised road declared across a wall, and T110-2 (1) an aqueduct drawn across one. A build whose re-shape dry run skips the wall check passes every bar, leaving a road deck carried over a curtain or an aqueduct pier in a band. That is an untested edge with a defined outcome on an editing path (principle (11); R6-01's grading).

claim: T110-2 (6)'s New random (base l. 18602–18605) reads: 'its seed searched so that the new ring's boundary meets one of the aqueduct's supports — the trace crossing the deck line under the nearest span, a support's edge its band meets built into the band'. At a regeneration, S3 lays that ring by the `EnceinteStrategy`'s pull. The crossing table's *beneath* (l. 2622–2625) says such a trace 'treats … an aqueduct's standing supports as impassable'. Only 'a stretch laid by neither' is 'bent locally … to cross an aqueduct under the nearest span (ties: the span nearer the deck's first foot in spine order)' (l. 2627–2631). The pull goes wherever its cost path and its 40 m search band take it, so 'the nearest span' is not its outcome. When the boundary meets the support at its centre, the two spans beside it tie, and the pull has no spine-order tie rule. So two units state two outcomes for one case. A test written from T110-2 checks for the nearest span, and a generator built to pass it would bend S3's regenerated trace locally, against *beneath* (R6-01: two units stating two outcomes for one case is MAJOR however rare the case).
required_change: §13.2's T110-2 (6): '— the trace crossing the deck line under the nearest span, a support's edge its band meets built into the band,' → '— the trace crossing the deck line under a span, never at a support, S3's pull treating the aqueduct's standing supports as impassable (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*), a support's edge its band meets built into the band,'.

claim: Two T110-2 clauses new this round read V04's arch vaults. T110-2 (4) (base l. 18570–18573) asserts that a hand `drawWall` across an aqueduct with a `vault` span in its line removes 'the `vault` span's arch vault … in the wall's commit (a fate in the hand dry run, the hand undo restoring it with the same id)'. T110-2 (1) (l. 18543) asserts 'a `vault` one read `open` with no chamber'. The arch vault and `ArchVaults.reconcile` land at V04's U3 (V04 l. 3207: 'the arch vaults and `ArchVaults.reconcile`'), inside M6-U, which §16 puts after M5. §13.8's T110 row (l. 19455) runs T110-2 at M3a. It names a later exit only for the epoch clauses (M4; M6-E's E2 and E3), and R6-09's sweep scheduled only those. Before U3 no arch vault exists, so (4)'s clause cannot run and (1)'s holds vacuously. INDEX §5 risk 2 and R5-05 (c) move such a clause to the first exit after its provider. V04's T-V4-63 runs the same case at its own step, so nothing built changes (VCS-r5-01's class, R6-09).
